Intermediate Catch Event

General Concept: An Intermediate Catch Event in BPMN is used to wait for a specific trigger (message, timer, signal, etc.) during process execution. It pauses the process until the event occurs.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, Intermediate Catch Events can be configured for various trigger types. The engine manages subscriptions and variable scope, and resumes the process when the event is caught. Input mappings using FEEL expressions can be used to process event data. Supports error handling and correlation for message events.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
An Intermediate Catch Event in TaktX allows you to:

  • Pause process execution until a specific event (message, timer, signal, etc.) occurs.
  • Configure event subscriptions and correlation for message events.
  • Define input mappings using FEEL expressions to process event data.
  • Set up error handling for unmatched or incorrect events.
  • Monitor event handling and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for event-driven process steps and external triggers.

 

Example: Customer Response Wait with Message Catch Event

 

This example shows a process where an Intermediate Catch Event waits for a customer response (Message Catch Event) before continuing. This demonstrates event-driven process control in TaktX.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions to process event data.
  • Configure correlation for message events.
  • Document expected triggers and outcomes.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmatched events will not trigger the process.
  • Incorrect correlation can block the process.
